name: Two protagonists, one story
subtitle: Switching between Jason and Lucia
summary: You play both leads. They can work a job together, with the game switching between them on the fly, or split up and roam Leonida separately.

facts.text: Players can play as Jason and Lucia together or set out on their own with either of them.
When the two are together, switching is near-instant mid-mission; when apart, each can be anywhere in the state and the swap plays out as a bird's-eye transition.
Some jobs are reportedly only available to one of the two characters.

name: Relationship system
subtitle: Jason and Lucia's bond
summary: How the two leads treat each other has a running effect on their relationship. It can strain, but reportedly can't be broken outright.

facts.text: Choices affect the relationship between Jason and Lucia, with ups and downs based on what the player does.
The relationship reportedly cannot be permanently broken regardless of player choices.
Rockstar's site describes hanging out with the other character as optional, not forced.

name: Criminal Profile
subtitle: Reputation system
summary: A running record of how heinous your crimes are, working quietly in the background like Red Dead Redemption 2's honour meter.

facts.text: Tracks the severity of the player's crimes and nudges how the world responds, in the style of RDR2's honour system.
An angel-style icon reportedly appears for kind acts, such as being good to animals.

name: Wanted system
subtitle: Five stars, smarter cops
summary: The five-star wanted level is back, with a few realism tweaks: stash your gun to stay unnoticed, and swap cars to slip a pursuit.

facts.text: The classic five-star wanted system returns largely intact.
Concealing weapons keeps NPCs from reacting, and changing vehicles can break police detection.

name: Carjacking
subtitle: More than one way in
summary: Stealing a parked car now depends on what you carry: a slim jim for a quiet entry or a smashed window for a fast, loud one.

facts.text: Multiple carjacking methods were shown — a shim/slim-jim for stealth and window-smashing for speed, tied to tools and progression.

name: Body, fitness and fatigue
subtitle: Your habits show
summary: Eat too much and you gain weight; hit the gym and fitness climbs; push too hard or skip sleep and it shows on your character's face.

facts.text: Both Jason and Lucia can gain or lose weight, and exercise raises fitness.
Overexertion causes fatigue, and sleep deprivation is reportedly visible on the characters.
Gym sessions, bench pressing, dining and character customisation (hair, clothes, accessories) were all shown.

name: NPC awareness
subtitle: The world notices you
summary: NPCs react to what you do and remember it. Linger to eavesdrop and they'll call you out; enemies are more dangerous than in past games.

facts.text: Rockstar says NPC interaction goes much further than Red Dead Redemption 2, including NPCs objecting when you listen in on them too long.
Rockstar warned that the player is not the only one capable of violence — enemies pose a bigger threat than before.
NPCs are reported to remember player actions.

name: Combat and gunplay
subtitle: Cover, slow-mo and melee
summary: Third-person cover shooting with a slow-motion focus mechanic carried over from RDR2, leg shots to disable enemies, shooting from car back seats and brutal hand-to-hand finishers.

facts.text: Refined cover-based shooting with peek-and-shoot, leg shots to disable, and shooting from a vehicle's rear seat.
A slow-motion aiming feature in the RDR2 style, plus improved dodging and melee finishing moves.
Shotguns can be fired one-handed while holding something else; improvised melee (including a stiletto heel) was shown.

name: In-game social media
subtitle: Doomscrolling in Leonida
summary: A phone full of parody social apps you can actually scroll, sending up 2020s feeds and livestream culture.

facts.text: Players can scroll in-game social platforms; crimes can even be livestreamed.
A Snapmatic-style app returns, parodying modern short-video apps.

name: Activities and side content
subtitle: More to do than ever
summary: Beyond missions: jet skis, scuba, airboats, basketball, boxing, gyms, clubs, racing, skydiving and more, spread across the state.

facts.text: The Extended Look showed jet skiing, kayaking, airboating, scooter riding, basketball, diving, gym workouts, swimming, VR, racing, boxing, dirt biking, base jumping, clubbing and dancing.
Parasailing and weightlifting were also shown.

name: Heists and robberies
subtitle: From gas stations to banks
summary: Small-scale stick-ups of convenience stores, gas stations and phone shops sit alongside bigger crew jobs with veteran robbers like Raul.

facts.text: Several robbery sequences (convenience store, gas station, phone shop) were shown in the Extended Look.
Rockstar's site lists heists among the things players will do.

name: Performance and tech
subtitle: 30 fps at launch
summary: Runs at 30 frames per second on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S at launch. A 60 fps mode has not been ruled out, but nothing is confirmed.

facts.text: Rockstar North's Rob Nelson said the consoles are currently running the game at 30 fps and that is the performance target for now.
Whether a 60 fps or performance mode arrives at launch or later is undecided; resolution, ray tracing and PS5 Pro specifics are unconfirmed.
Rockstar says no generative AI was used to make the game, and there are no microtransactions in single-player.
Main story length is reported at roughly 80 hours.
